title: Security Metrics and Reporting
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 6: Security Assessment and Testing: Security Metrics and Reporting.

items: KPIs measure how well security objectives are being achieved
Quantifiable metrics tied to organizational goals
Examples: mean time to patch, percentage of systems scanned, training completion rate
Must be meaningful, measurable, and actionable
Reported to management regularly

blocks.text: From the Official CBK: "KPIs—Key Performance Indicators" are one of two critical types of security metrics, along with KRIs. Common security KPIs:

items: Mean time to detect (MTTD) — How quickly threats are detected
Mean time to respond (MTTR) — How quickly incidents are addressed
Patch compliance rate — Percentage of systems patched within SLA
Vulnerability scan coverage — Percentage of assets scanned
Security awareness training completion — Percentage of employees trained
False positive rate — Accuracy of detection tools

blocks.text: From the Official CBK: "Management review and approval metrics typically focus on products and processes, including the review and approval process itself. Things like 'time to resolve defects,' 'number of defects identified,' 'defect detection effectiveness,' 'average cost per defect.'"

items: KRIs provide early warning of increasing risk
Leading indicators that predict potential security issues
Examples: number of unpatched critical systems, failed login attempts, expired certificates
Trigger proactive risk management actions
Different from KPIs (KPIs measure performance; KRIs measure risk)

blocks.text: From the Official CBK: "Two types of metrics are very important: KPIs—Key Performance Indicators and KRIs—Key Risk Indicators." KPI vs KRI:

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: KPIs are LAGGING indicators (measuring past performance). KRIs are LEADING indicators (predicting future risk). Both are essential but serve different purposes.

items: Security reports must be tailored to the audience
Executive reports — High-level risk posture, trends, business impact
Technical reports — Detailed findings, CVEs, remediation steps
Compliance reports — Adherence to regulatory requirements
Reports should include trends (improving or worsening over time)

blocks.text: From the Official CBK: Incident Response Measurement should include:

items: Involved Parties: CIO, CISO
Data Source: Incident logs, incident tracking database
Reporting Format: Line chart that illustrates individual categories

blocks.text: Metrics should be specific to the audience — "what do they want to see, what do they need to know." ⚠️ Exam Trap: Report to executives in BUSINESS terms (risk, cost, impact), not technical terms (CVE numbers, port numbers). A CISO presenting to the board should say "we reduced breach risk by 40%" not "we patched 500 CVEs."
